candidate.title: TruSeq RNA Stranded
candidate.scope: The single Illumina product-preparation schematic titled TruSeq RNA Stranded: depicted RNA and random primer through first cDNA synthesis, dUTP-marked second-strand synthesis, grouped end preparation, adapter ligation, and strand-selective amplification to an indexed product ready for cluster generation. No alternative target workflow is depicted. This is a schematic-level architecture, not a complete protocol or a claim about every TruSeq product version. The nonproductive U-marked template is retained as a branch within the final block. No upstream RNA isolation, enrichment or fragmentation, nor downstream cluster-generation or sequencing operation, is supplied by this panel.

features: Purple RNA strand is labelled 5′ at left and 3′ at right.
A short blue random primer is shown below the RNA; no upstream RNA selection or fragmentation is depicted.

states.label: Double-stranded cDNA with a uracil-marked sense strand

The RNA template is no longer drawn at this stage; its removal mechanism is not specified.

features: The final molecule is drawn as one horizontal line with a blue insert.

The stated endpoint is readiness for cluster generation; cluster formation and sequencing are not drawn.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Adapters are attached at both ends of the end-prepared insert, producing the forked adapter-bearing duplex. The adapter arms carry the depicted P5/P7 and Index 1/Index 2 segments; U marks remain in the sense strand.
operations.mechanism: Adapter ligation is explicitly labelled; no ligase identity or detailed adapter chemistry is provided.
operations.information_effect: Index-labelled and P5/P7-labelled adapter segments become physically linked to the RNA-derived insert. The figure supplies no index-to-sample assignment.

evidence.locator: Adaptor ligation: arrow to forked adapters at both ends; P5, P7, Index 1, Index 2 and Sense strand labels

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: The adapter-bearing duplex is denatured into the two drawn strands. In the same depicted block, polymerase copying of the U-bearing sense strand is blocked, while the unmarked first-strand template supports amplification leading to the indexed DNA product shown below. The blocked strand is retained here as a nonproductive branch, not assigned an unshown degradation step.
operations.mechanism: The source explicitly labels the U-containing separated strand Block polymerase; it does not name the polymerase or show uracil excision. Denaturation and amplification remain a single source-labelled block.
operations.information_effect: Selective copying preserves which RNA-derived cDNA strand was first synthesized: the final amplifiable library derives from the unmarked first-strand template rather than productive copying of both original cDNA strands. The DNA insert carries the RNA sequence representation, while the depicted strand asymmetry supports strand-of-origin information. No sequencing-read orientation, quantitative expression readout or performance guarantee is established by this panel.
